key_facts: France has a national AI strategy that is part of the broader France 2030 investment plan.
The France 2030 plan is a €54 billion investment plan for innovation, industrialization, and research.
Approximately €1 billion was committed to AI development for the period 2022-2025 as part of the national AI strategy.
A further €2 billion is planned for AI investment before the end of the France 2030 plan, totaling €4 billion in public AI investments.
France aims to build a competitive and sovereign technology offering in AI, focusing on embedded AI, trustworthy AI, frugal AI, and generative AI.
Measures were added in 2023 to the national AI strategy to address the rapid development of generative AI.
France is a leading European country for foreign investments in AI, attracting 41 AI-related projects in 2024.
French AI startups raised €1.9 billion in 2024.
France ranks third globally in terms of AI researchers.

France has implemented an ambitious national AI strategy since 2018, divided into phases: Phase 1 (2018-2022) focused on structuring research (€1.5 billion), and Phase 2 (since 2022) focuses on accelerating innovation with €1 billion granted.
Bpifrance is deploying €10 billion to develop the AI ecosystem and facilitate AI adoption by French companies.
Over €3.4 billion in financing for innovative AI projects is planned by Bpifrance by the end of 2024 through specific France 2030 calls for projects.
Iliad has committed over €3 billion to its AI strategy, including a strategic alliance for data centers and increasing Scaleway's GPU capacity.
France aims to become an AI powerhouse, as evidenced by initiatives like the €109 billion in private AI investment mentioned by Nico Rosberg, contrasting with the US's €500 billion investment.
